visaPathways.title: Visa Pathways in Spain
visaPathways.overview: Spain offers several immigration pathways for individuals, families, students, and entrepreneurs looking to make Spain their new home. The right visa or residence permit will depend on your goals, whether you're planning to work, study, join family members, or establish your own business.

blocks.text: The Non-Lucrative Visa is one of the most popular pathways for individuals and families who want to live in Spain without working for a Spanish employer.
This visa may be a good fit for:

items: Individuals living from savings or investments
Those taking a sabbatical or planning a lifestyle move to Spain

blocks.text: To qualify, applicants generally need to demonstrate sufficient financial resources to support themselves and any dependent family members, along with private health insurance and a clean criminal record.

items: Proof of sufficient financial means — you’ll need to show stable savings or passive income to support yourself (and any dependents) without working in Spain.
Private health insurance — full-coverage Spanish health insurance with no co-payments is required for the duration of your stay.
Clean criminal record — background checks from your country (or countries) of residence for the past five years.
Medical certificate — confirmation that you do not have any illnesses that pose a public health risk under international regulations.
No employment in Spain — this visa is designed for those who will not work for a Spanish employer.

Apply from your home country — the initial application must be submitted through the Spanish consulate where you legally reside. Our team at Hola España handles the document preparation and coordinates the submission process, so everything is organized, accurate, and stress-free from start to finish.

blocks.text: The Non-Lucrative Visa does not authorize employment in Spain. However, many people use this pathway as a first step toward long-term residency while enjoying Spain's lifestyle, culture, and quality of life.
The visa is typically granted for one year initially and may be renewed, eventually creating a pathway toward long-term residence in Spain.
Spain's Digital Nomad Visa was created for remote workers and freelancers who want to live in Spain while working for employers or clients located outside the country.
This visa may be a good fit for:

items: Remote employees working for foreign companies

blocks.text: This visa may also be a good fit for:

items: Remote employees of foreign companies — professionals working for a non-Spanish employer with authorization to work remotely from Spain.
Freelancers or independent contractors — individuals providing services primarily to clients located outside of Spain.
Business owners or entrepreneurs — those running an established company abroad and managing it remotely.
Tech and knowledge-based professionals — specialists in fields like IT, marketing, consulting, design, finance, and other digital industries who can perform their work fully online.

blocks.text: Applicants generally need to demonstrate a stable source of income, professional qualifications or relevant work experience, and the ability to perform their work remotely. Private health insurance and a clean criminal record are also typically required.
For many remote professionals, the Digital Nomad Visa offers a flexible pathway to Spanish residency while continuing to work with international employers and clients.
The visa is typically granted for one to three years initially and may be renewed, eventually creating a pathway toward long-term residence in Spain.
For entrepreneurs, freelancers, and business owners who wish to live and work in Spain by operating their own business.
This residence permit may be suitable if you plan to:

items: Launch a new business in Spain
Work as a freelancer or independent contractor

blocks.text: Applicants are generally required to present a viable business plan, demonstrate sufficient financial resources, and show that the proposed activity complies with Spanish regulations.
This pathway allows you to live and work legally in Spain while building your own business.
If you already have close family members legally residing in Spain, you may be able to join them through Spain's family reunification process.
Family reunification may be available for:

The sponsoring family member must generally demonstrate adequate housing, financial means, and legal residence status in Spain. Once approved, family members can obtain residence authorization and, in many cases, access employment opportunities in Spain.
For individuals who have secured employment with a Spanish employer.
This pathway is commonly used by:

items: Individuals accepting a job offer from a Spanish company

blocks.text: In most cases, the employer begins the application process by obtaining work authorization on behalf of the employee. Once approved, the applicant can obtain the appropriate visa and residence permit to live and work in Spain. Initial permits are typically granted for one year and may be renewed.

subsections.title: Residence Permit for Study or Research (Student visa)

blocks.text: For students, researchers, and academics pursuing educational or research opportunities in Spain.
This permit may be appropriate for:

Applicants generally must be accepted into an approved educational institution or research program and demonstrate sufficient financial means and health insurance coverage. Depending on the circumstances, certain permits may also allow limited work activities or pathways to longer-term residence after studies are completed.

subsections.title: Family Members of an EU Citizen

blocks.text: Non-EU family members of European Union, EEA, or Swiss citizens may have access to a special residence pathway when accompanying or joining their qualifying family member in Spain.

segments.text: Family of EU Citizen Spanish Visa Explained

blocks.text: This route may apply to:
Eligible family members can apply for a residence card that allows them to reside in Spain alongside their EU family member and, in many cases, access employment and other residency rights.

taxes.title: Taxes in Spain
taxes.overview: Understanding your tax obligations is an important part of relocating to Spain. Tax rules can vary depending on your residency status, income sources, assets, and investments. The overview below highlights some of the most common tax considerations for individuals, property owners, and business operators.

blocks.text: Your tax obligations in Spain will depend largely on whether you are considered a tax resident or non-resident.

items: Income Tax (IRPF): Spanish tax residents are generally taxed on their worldwide income.
Non-Resident Tax: Non-residents may only be taxed on income earned within Spain.
Wealth Tax: Individuals with significant assets may be subject to wealth tax depending on their circumstances and region of residence.
Tax Residency: Generally, spending more than 183 days per year in Spain may result in tax residency status.

blocks.text: Spain requires various tax filings depending on your residency status, assets, and business activities.

items: Form 720: Declaration of certain assets held outside Spain.
Form 210: Commonly used by non-residents to report taxable income and property ownership obligations.
Income Tax Returns: Annual filings for tax residents.
Corporate Tax Returns: Required for companies operating within Spain.

blocks.text: Owning property in Spain may create additional tax obligations.

items: Real Estate Taxes: Property owners may be responsible for local property taxes and other municipal charges.
Capital Gains Tax: May apply when selling Spanish property or other qualifying assets.
Rental Income Tax: Income earned from renting property may be subject to taxation.
Property Ownership Requirements: Tax responsibilities can vary based on residency status and property usage.

blocks.text: Spain applies taxes to certain transfers of wealth, though rates and exemptions can vary by region.

segments.text: Inheritance and Gift Tax in Spain Explained

items: Inheritance Tax: May apply when assets are inherited by beneficiaries.
Gift Tax: Can apply when money, property, or other assets are gifted during a person's lifetime.
Donations: Certain charitable donations may have tax implications or available deductions.
Regional Differences: Tax rates and allowances often vary between Spain's autonomous communities.

blocks.text: Starting a business in Spain involves selecting the appropriate legal structure, registering the company, obtaining tax identification numbers, and complying with local and national regulations.
